PHP is mainly focused on server-side scripting, so it can do anything any other CGI program can do, such as collect form data, generate dynamic page content, or send and receive cookies.

When PHP processes a file, it recognizes the opening and closing tags, <?php and ?>, to define the boundaries of PHP code execution. Content outside these tags is ignored by the PHP parser. If a file ends with PHP code, it is preferable to omit the PHP closing tag at the end of the file.

The closing tag of a PHP block at the end of a file is optional. The closing tag of a block of PHP code automatically implies a semicolon; you do not need to have a semicolon terminating the last line of a PHP block.
echo is not a function but a language construct. Its arguments are a list of expressions following the echo keyword, separated by commas, and not delimited by parentheses.

There is no int division operator in PHP. To achieve this, use the intdiv() function. 1/2 yields the float 0.5. var_dump(25/7); // float(3.5714285714286)
Determine if a variable is declared and is different than null. isset() will return false when checking a variable that has been assigned to null.

sources.excerpt: for loops are the most complex loops in PHP. The syntax of a for loop is: for (expr1; expr2; expr3) statement. The first expression (expr1) is evaluated (executed) once unconditionally at the beginning of the loop.

The meaning of a while statement is simple. It tells PHP to execute the nested statement(s) repeatedly, as long as the while expression evaluates to true. The value of the expression is checked each time at the beginning of the loop.

do-while loops are very similar to while loops, except the truth expression is checked at the end of each iteration instead of in the beginning. The main difference from regular while loops is that the first iteration of a do-while loop is guaranteed to run.

break ends execution of the current for, foreach, while, do-while or switch structure. break accepts an optional numeric argument which tells it how many nested enclosing structures are to be broken out of.
continue is used within looping structures to skip the rest of the current loop iteration and continue execution at the condition evaluation and then the beginning of the next iteration.
count — Counts all elements in an array or in a Countable object. Returns the number of elements in value. When used with an array, counts all elements in the array.

sources.excerpt: The visibility of a property, a method or (as of PHP 7.1.0) a constant can be defined by prefixing the declaration with public, protected or private. Class members declared public can be accessed everywhere. Members declared protected can be accessed only within the class itself and by inheriting and parent classes. Members declared as private may only be accessed by the class that defines the member.

As of PHP 8.0.0, constructor parameters may also be promoted to correspond to an object property. It is very common for constructor parameters to be assigned to a property. Promotion combines declaration and assignment.
Declaring class properties or methods as static makes them accessible without needing an instantiation of the class. These can also be accessed statically within an instantiated class object.
It is possible to define constants on a per-class basis. The default visibility of class constants is public.

Namespaces are a way of encapsulating items to avoid name collisions. PHP Namespaces provide a way in which to group related classes, interfaces, functions and constants.

To obtain the fully qualified name of a class ClassName use ClassName::class. Example in namespace NS: echo ClassName::class; output: NS\ClassName (no leading backslash). As of PHP 8.0.0, ::class may also be used on objects; its effect is the same as calling get_class() on the object.

sources.excerpt: Object interfaces allow you to create code which specifies which methods and properties a class must implement, without having to define how these methods or properties are implemented. Classes defined as abstract cannot be instantiated, and any class that contains at least one abstract method or property must also be abstract. Methods defined as abstract simply declare the method's signature; they cannot define the implementation. When inheriting from an abstract class, all methods marked abstract in the parent's class declaration must be defined by the child class.

sources.excerpt: Traits are a mechanism for code reuse in single inheritance languages such as PHP. A Trait is similar to a class, but only intended to group functionality. It is not possible to instantiate a Trait on its own. To resolve naming conflicts between Traits used in the same class, the insteadof operator needs to be used. The as operator can be used to add an alias.

If two Traits insert a method with the same name, a fatal error is produced, if the conflict is not explicitly resolved. To resolve naming conflicts, the insteadof operator needs to be used to choose exactly one of the conflicting methods. The as operator can be used to add an alias to one of the methods.

sources.excerpt: To specify the type of an array like [1, 2, 3], you can use the syntax number[]; this syntax works for any type (e.g. string[] is an array of strings). You may also see this written as Array<number>, which means the same thing.
A tuple type is another sort of Array type that knows exactly how many elements it contains, and exactly which types it contains at specific positions.

sources.excerpt: An interface declaration is another way to name an object type. TypeScript is only concerned with the structure of the value we passed - it only cares that it has the expected properties. Being concerned only with the structure and capabilities of types is why we call TypeScript a structurally typed type system.

Much of the time, we'll find ourselves dealing with objects that might have a property set. In those cases, we can mark those properties as optional by adding a question mark (?) to the end of their names. Properties can also be marked as readonly for TypeScript.

sources.excerpt: A union type is a type formed from two or more other types, representing values that may be any one of those types. TypeScript will only allow an operation if it is valid for every member of the union.
When every type in a union contains a common property with literal types, TypeScript considers that to be a discriminated union, and can narrow out the members of the union.

sources.excerpt: The unknown type represents any value. This is similar to the any type, but is safer because it's not legal to do anything with an unknown value.

sources.excerpt: TypeScript offers special syntax for turning a constructor parameter into a class property with the same name and value. These are called parameter properties and are created by prefixing a constructor argument with one of the visibility modifiers public, private, protected, or readonly.

The default visibility of class members is public. protected members are only visible to subclasses of the class they're declared in. private is like protected, but doesn't allow access to the member even from subclasses.

sources.excerpt: In modern TypeScript, you may not need an enum when an object with as const could suffice. The biggest argument in favour of this format over TypeScript's enum is that it keeps your codebase aligned with the state of JavaScript.

Enums are a feature added to JavaScript by TypeScript which allows for describing a value which could be one of a set of possible named constants. Because of this, it's a feature which you should know exists, but maybe hold off on using unless you are sure.

sources.excerpt: We've now added a type variable Type to the identity function. This Type allows us to capture the type the user provides (e.g. number), so that we can use that information later. Unlike using any, it's also just as precise.

Instead of working with any and all types, we'd like to constrain this function to work with any and all types that also have the .length property. We'll use this interface and the extends keyword to denote our constraint.

sources.excerpt: The sender broadcasts an ARP request: who-has TARGET-PROTOCOL-ADDRESS? The target unicasts an ARP reply containing its hardware address. Ethernet broadcast destination is FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF.
An IP host group address is mapped to an Ethernet multicast address by placing the low-order 23 bits of the IP address into the low-order 23 bits of the Ethernet multicast address 01-00-5E-00-00-00.
An IPv6 packet with a multicast destination address DST is transmitted to the Ethernet multicast address whose first two octets are 33-33 and whose last four octets are the last four octets of DST.
IEEE 802.1Q defined the VLAN Identifier (VID) as a 12-bit field, supporting up to 4094 VLANs (VID 0 and 4095 are reserved).
ip link add link DEVICE name NAME type vlan [ protocol VLAN_PROTO ] id VLANID ... id VLANID specifies the VLAN Identifier to use.

Wi-Fi 6 is based on IEEE 802.11ax (2019) and Wi-Fi 6E adds the 6 GHz band (2021). Wi-Fi 5 is 802.11ac (5 GHz). The Alliance later mapped earlier PHYs: 802.11n as Wi-Fi 4, 802.11g as Wi-Fi 3, 802.11a as Wi-Fi 2, 802.11b as Wi-Fi 1.

sources.excerpt: IPv6 addresses are 128-bit identifiers. The preferred form is x:x:x:x:x:x:x:x. The use of "::" indicates one or more groups of 16 bits of zeros. TShark's native capture file format is pcapng. -f capture filter, -Y display filter. sources.title: The Merge

sources.excerpt: The Merge was executed on September 15, 2022. sources.excerpt: There is a base fee per gas in protocol, which can move up or down each block according to a formula. The base fee per gas is burned.
